concerns.text: Task T008 is marked [X] (complete) but contains a 'SKIPPED' comment and a YAML parsing error in its description. This task is the sole source of the ground truth reference data required by SC-003 (exact match for n<=100). Its failure to produce `tests/data/reference_values.csv` means the verification step for FR-001/SC-003 is impossible, constituting a dropped acceptance criterion.

Task T004 requires saving primes to `code/utils/primes.npy`, but T016a (feature engineering) and T011 (partition generation) rely on this file. T004 is marked [ ] (incomplete). Downstream tasks (T011, T016a) are marked [X] or dependent on T004, creating a semantic violation where the deliverable (primes.npy) does not exist to satisfy the dependency chain required by FR-001 and FR-004.

Task T013 (validation logic to skip n where p_P(n)=0) is marked [ ] (incomplete). However, FR-003 and SC-003 explicitly require handling edge cases where p_P(n)=0 gracefully before log-residual calculation. Without T013, the pipeline will crash on log(0) or produce invalid residuals, violating the acceptance criteria for FR-003.

Tasks T031 and T032 are marked [ ] (incomplete) but are labeled 'Research-Stage Revision' addressing critical concerns about the generating function definition and asymptotic regime. The spec (FR-002) and plan mandate the use of the distinct-partition variant of Meinardus' theorem. Without T031 (documenting the generating function) and T032 (defining n_max regime), the implementation risks using the wrong asymptotic baseline or undefined scope, violating the 'Verified Accuracy' and 'Finite-Regime Error Term Precision' constitutional principles.

Task T016b (validate features.csv) is marked [ ] (incomplete). FR-004 requires generating specific predictor variables (distance to nearest prime, oscillatory terms). T016a generates them, but T016b is the explicit verification step ensuring they are 'present and non-null' before regression. Skipping T016b means the acceptance criterion for FR-004 (valid predictors) is not verified, risking a silent failure in the regression model.
